gloss: Loyal, covenant love — God's steadfast commitment to his people that endures regardless of their faithfulness. Broader than 'mercy' or 'kindness' alone; it implies an ongoing relational obligation.
Wholeness, completeness, well-being — not merely absence of conflict but everything being as it should be, in right relationship with God, others, and creation.
Spirit, breath, or wind — the same word covers all three. God's ruach is both his life-giving breath and his personal presence (e.g. Gen 1:2).
The whole living self — not a disembodied 'soul' in the Greek sense, but a person as a breathing, embodied living being.
Instruction or teaching — often translated 'law,' but broader: God's guidance for how to live, not merely a legal code.
A binding agreement, often sealed with a sign or ritual, establishing mutual obligations between God and his people (e.g. with Noah, Abraham, Israel, David).
Right relationship and right conduct — living rightly toward God and community, not just individual moral rectitude.
Set apart, distinct from the ordinary — God's essential otherness, and by extension what is consecrated for his purposes.
Literally 'missing the mark' — falling short of a standard or target, whether through defiance or failure.
Weightiness, substance, honor — God's kabod is the visible, weighty manifestation of his presence and worth.
Firmness, reliability, truth — often paired with hesed to describe God as steadfastly loving and utterly dependable.
To rescue, deliver, bring into a spacious/safe place — the root behind the names Joshua and Jesus (Yeshua).
God — grammatically plural in form but used with singular verbs for the one God of Israel; conveys fullness of deity and majesty.
To remember — in Scripture this is active, not just mental recall: when God 'remembers' a covenant, he acts on it.
Reverent awe and submission before God's holiness — not mere terror, though it can include it; the beginning of wisdom (Prov 9:10).
To create — used in the Old Testament exclusively with God as subject, denoting creation that only he can accomplish.
Skill for living — practical, God-oriented competence in navigating life rightly, not mere intellectual knowledge.
To kneel, to bless — invoking favor and empowerment for flourishing, moving in both directions between God and people.
Anointed one — set apart by anointing with oil for a God-given office (king, priest, prophet); root of 'Messiah' and (via Greek) 'Christ.'
Servant or slave — used both of lowly service and as an honorific title for those in God's special service (e.g. 'servant of the LORD').
Self-giving, willed love that seeks the good of another regardless of merit or return — distinct from phileo (affectionate friendship) and eros (romantic desire).
Word, reason, message — in John 1, the eternal self-expression of God, personified and identified as Christ.
Unearned favor and gift — God's generosity toward those who have not earned it and could not repay it.
Trust, faithfulness, allegiance — more than intellectual assent; a whole-life reliance on and loyalty to God.
Righteousness/justice — right standing before God and right conduct; in Paul, often the righteous status God grants through faith in Christ.
Rescue, deliverance, wholeness — salvation understood as comprehensive rescue from sin, death, and judgment into new life.
Assembly, called-out gathering — originally a civic term for a citizens' assembly, repurposed for the gathered people of God.
Good news — originally announcing a victory or a king's accession; in the NT, the announcement of God's saving reign in Christ.
A change of mind leading to a change of direction — not mere regret, but a fundamental reorientation of life toward God.
Missing the mark — falling short of God's standard, whether by a single act or as a settled condition/power at work in a person.
Splendor, honor, radiant presence — the visible weight and worth of God, later also used of the honor believers will share in Christ.
Spirit, breath, wind — the Greek counterpart to ruach; the Holy Spirit as God's personal, life-giving presence and power.
Flesh — can mean simply the physical body, but in Paul often denotes fallen human nature in rebellion against God, opposed to Spirit-led living.
The ordered world/humanity — can be neutral (creation) or negative (humanity organized in opposition to God), depending on context.
Kingdom, reign, rule — less a place than God's active, dynamic reign breaking into the world through Christ.
Shared life, partnership, participation — deep mutual belonging among believers, and with God, not mere social association.
The place/means of atonement — the mercy seat in the OT tabernacle, and in Rom 3:25 the means by which Christ's death turns aside God's wrath and covers sin.
End, goal, culmination — not merely a stopping point but the intended purpose toward which something is moving (e.g. Christ as the telos of the law, Rom 10:4).
Arrival, presence — used of Christ's promised return, and originally of a king's official state visit to a city.
Anointed One — the Greek translation of Hebrew Mashiach; not a surname but a title identifying Jesus as God's promised king.
Covenant or will/testament — the binding arrangement God establishes with his people, climactically renewed in Christ's blood (Luke 22:20).
